thread:
amanda: Heads-up — after the mkdocs -> docusaurus migration a bunch of intra-doc anchors under /guides/installer are 404ing in prod. Got two user reports this morning.
kyle: Which pages specifically?
amanda: https://docs.redwood.ai/guides/installer#quickstart and https://docs.redwood.ai/guides/installer#service-accounts — clicking the header links just jumps to the top of the page.
maria: CI linkcheck caught similar ones. Failure snippet: 'ERROR: Fragment not found: #service-accounts (in /guides/installer)'. I saw this on the nightly build.
docs-bot: linkcheck: 5 broken fragments found in build 4321. Full report: https://ci.redwood.dev/build/4321/output
kyle: Quick hypothesis — some headings ended up inside MDX/html wrappers during migration, which changes slug generation. Also we had a few heading-level changes (### -> ##) in the conversion script.
amanda: Are these easy to fix? We have external links to some anchors from older blog posts.
maria: Two paths: 1) add explicit heading ids where we rely on stable anchors: e.g., `## Service accounts {#service-accounts}` in MDX; 2) add a redirect map plugin in Docusaurus that maps old-fragment -> new-fragment so old links survive.
nick: Redirects are nice for external links. For internal refs we should probably fix the source headings too (explicit IDs) so linkcheck is happy and content is canonical.
kyle: There's another wrinkle: some headings ended up as text inside fenced code blocks because of a botched code-fence conversion, so the anchor disappears entirely. Example from installer.md:

```
    ### Service accounts
    Copy these creds...
```

That indentation turned the heading into indented code block in MDX, so the slug never existed.
amanda: Oof. So for those we need a content fix (unindent) not a redirect.
maria: I'll run a quick grep to find headings in indented blocks: `rg "^\s{4,}#{1,6} " docs/guides | sed -n '1,200p'` and then submit a PR with fixes for the installer guide.
docs-bot: CI: linkcheck failing for docs/guides/installer — 3 fragments missing. See https://ci.redwood.dev/build/4321/linkcheck
kyle: Could we add a small post-migration script to normalise slugs and produce a compatibility redirect table? That would catch weird edge cases without manual edits.
nick: I can prototype a slugmap generator. It will scan git history for old headings and current headings, diff slugs, and emit a JSON used by the docusaurus-redirects plugin.
amanda: That sounds ideal. In parallel I'll manually patch the most egregious installer headings (quick fix) so users stop hitting 404s.
maria: I'll open a PR for the manual patches (installer fixes + a couple explicit `{#id}`s in api/reference where external links are common).
amanda: Please add a small note in the PR description about why we can't rely on implicit slugs post-migration.
kyle: Also add a tiny linkcheck unit test in `.github/actions/linkcheck` to assert that known anchors (e.g., `#service-accounts`) exist after the change.
nick: I opened a draft proto for slugmap here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1423 — contains generator and sample redirects JSON. It's WIP.
maria: Thanks — I'll review and add the installer patch into that PR if it's ok.
amanda: Great. Can someone also update the release notes checklist: "verify docs anchors + linkcheck" so we don't regress in future migration steps?
kyle: Added to checklist in the docs repo. :thumbsup:

amanda: OK team — action items: maria -> run grep & push manual fixes; nick -> iterate on slugmap; kyle -> add unit in linkcheck; I'll coordinate release note update and merge order. Ping here when PRs are ready.
maria: On it, will aim for a PR today.
nick: I'll convert my draft to a proper PR tomorrow and add tests. :coffee:
docs-bot: Reminder: nightly build scheduled at 02:00 UTC — linkcheck will re-run after merges.
